prerequisites: Familiarity with concepts associated with functions (domain, range)
Basic knowledge of set theory and relations

learning_outcomes.text: Express a real situation or problem using a graph
Construct Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths in the corresponding graphs
Use trees and their properties as a data structure
Solve real problems using graph theory
Construct a finite automaton recognizing a given simple language and describe the regular language associated with a small given finite automaton
Relate regular languages to regular expressions and equivalent automata
Recognize the limits of languages that can be recognized by finite automata
Describe some application of finite automata
Construct simple grammars generating a given language and determine the language generated by a grammar
Simplify a given context-free grammar and transform it into any of the normal forms
Recognize context-free languages and know their formal properties
Describe some application of context-free grammars
Design a simple Turing Machine associated with a given language
Reproduce the Chomsky hierarchy related to formal languages

syllabus_topics: Autómatas Finitos No Determinísticos (AFN) y su equivalencia con los AFD
AFN con lambda-movimientos (AFN-λ) y su equivalencia con los AFN
Expresiones regulares (ER) y su equivalencia con los Autómatas Finitos
Propiedades formales de los Lenguajes regulares
Autómatas, gramáticas y lenguajes libres de contexto
Gramáticas regulares y su equivalencia con los Autómatas Finitos
Gramáticas y lenguajes libres de contexto (GLC, LLC)
Formas Normales de Chomsky y Greibach
Introducción al análisis léxico y sintáctico en compiladores
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for each partial exam (T1, T2, T3). The final grade for each topic (T1, T2, T3) will be the maximum between the partial exam score and the corresponding part in the official call's theoretical exam. The final grade is calculated as (0.90 * ((T1 + T2 + T3) / 3)) + (0.10 * CL), provided all minimums are met; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. In the extraordinary call, there is a single theoretical exam divided into parts (TE1, TE2, TE3), each requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10 points; the final grade for each topic is the maximum between the extraordinary exam part and the ordinary exam part. The final grade is (TE1 + TE2 + TE3) / 3, provided all minimums are met; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0.
